The (Fe62Ni16Co9Mn9Ti4)100-xSix (x = 0, 3) Fe-HEAs were arc-melted in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon protective atmosphere.
The ingots were held at 1150 ◦C for 5 hours and subsequently water-quenched.
The homogenized ingots were then subjected to room temperature rolling with a reduction of 50 %, resulting in a final thickness of 6 mm.
Then the cold-rolled sheets were reheated to 1000 ◦C in an argon-protected furnace and held for 30 minutes before water quenching to room temperature.
The heat-treated sheets were further rolled at cryogenic temperature (-196 ◦C) with a reduction of 70 %
followed by annealing at 700 ◦C for 10 minutes and water quenching to room temperature.

The dislocation strengthening induced by high-density dislocations from cryogenic rolling cannot be neglected in the 3Si alloy.

Annealing after cryogenic rolling promotes significant recrystallization in the 3Si alloy, effectively refining the average grain size of the alloy and thus resulting in effective grain boundary strengthening.
